data: Binance spot 1-minute bars, 2020-01-01 to 2025-12-31 UTC. A = 2020-2024 (the direction comes from A), B = 2025 (every *_B number).
fires: A row fires at a minute close when its `when` event fires at that close (as in the traded pack) AND every reading in `conds` holds the given level at the last CLOSED bar of its own timeframe (oracle.heat_live.active_keys(..., states=...)). UTC4h is the 4-hour UTC block of the entry minute. The measured entry is the open of the next minute.
rule: Every pair and triple cell the tables stored, with a sample on both periods; no pass mark is used as a filter. Per coin and horizon: the top 40 by oheat_B and the top 20 by lheat_B, at most 3 rows of one trigger in each list. rank_coin / rank_lift_coin: among all distinct pair and triple events of the coin at that horizon. Identical events are one row (aliases).

units.oheat_B: windows per day x odds points
units.lift_B: odds points over the trigger's other events
units.rest_wd_B: windows per day of the trigger's other events
units.lheat_B: lift_B x the smaller of wd_B and rest_wd_B
units.lift2_B: odds points over the condition level's own effect
units.share_B: % of events beyond the entry on the called side at the horizon
units.odds_B: points (half the shift in P(up) - P(down))
units.trigger: the `when` event on its own at the same horizon (rank_coin: its rank in the traded pack, when it is in it)
units.hot_A / replicated_B: the league's own marks (information, not a filter)

limits: Only relationships with a cell that was hot on A were stored (per coin at most the strongest by lift on A), and the 170 strongest triggers per coin were crossed with every reading; every other event level only with the clock and dominance states. Rows of one trigger are close relatives.
